AN ACT to amend the general business law, in relation to requiring
peer-to-peer car sharing programs provide certain insurance coverage
items.lawCode: Amd §§901 & 905, Gen Bus L; amd §2131, Ins L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S5941

SPONSOR: SKOUFIS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the general business law, in relation to requiring peer-
to-peer car sharing programs provide certain insurance coverage

 
PURPOSE:

This bill modifies insurance requirements for peer-to-peer car-sharing
programs.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Amends subdivision 2 of section 901 of the general business
law, stating that peer-to-peer car-sharing companies shall provide
insurance coverage equal to the financial responsibility requirements
outlined in section 311 of the vehicle and traffic law. Removes the
requirement that peer-to-peer car-sharing programs maintain additional
liability insurance of at least $1.25 million for bodily injury, death,
or property damage. This section also removes the requirement for
supplementary uninsured/underinsured motorist insurance coverage of
$1.25 million per occurrence.

Section 2: Sets effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

This change brings insurance requirements for the peer-to-peer car-shar-
ing industry in line with traditional rental car companies, creating
parity between the industries. This ensures that peer-to-peer car-shar-
ing programs are not subject to stricter requirements than rental car
companies.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the ninetieth day after it shall have
become a law. Effective immediately, the addition, amendment and/or
repeal of any rule or regulation necessary for the implementation of
this act on its effective date are authorized to be made and completed
on or before such effective date.

BILL NUMBER: S5941A

SPONSOR: SKOUFIS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the general business law and the insurance law, in
relation to requiring peer-to-peer car sharing programs provide certain
insurance coverage

 
PURPOSE:

This bill modifies insurance requirements for peer-to-peer car-sharing
programs.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Amends subdivision 2 of section 901 of the general business
law, stating that peer-to-peer car-sharing companies shall provide
insurance coverage equal to the financial responsibility requirements
outlined in section 311 of the vehicle and traffic law. Removes the
requirement that peer-to-peer car-sharing programs maintain additional
liability insurance of at least $1.25 million for bodily injury, death,
or property damage. This section also removes the requirement for
supplementary uninsured/underinsured motorist insurance coverage of
$1.25 million per occurrence.

Section 2: Adds new subdivision 8 to section 901 of the general business
law which states that peer-to-peer car sharing programs must provide the
shared vehicle owner and shared vehicle driver the opportunity to
purchase additional insurance.

Section 3: Amends subdivision 1 of section 905 of the general business
law to add to the peer-to-peer car sharing agreement disclosures infor-
mation about the insurance available.

Section 4: Amends section 2131 of the insurance law to authorize peer to
peer car sharing administrators to provide insurance in the same manner
as rental car companies.

Section 5: Sets effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

This change brings insurance requirements for the peer-to-peer car-shar-
ing industry in line with traditional rental car companies, creating
parity between the industries. This ensures that peer-to-peer car-shar-
ing programs are not subject to stricter requirements than rental car
companies.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the one hundred eightieth day after it
shall have become a law. Effective immediately, the addition, amendment,
and/or repeal of any rule or regulation necessary for the implementation
of this act on its effective date are authorized to be made and
completed on or before such effective date.

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 73 Chapter 696
 
       MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 5941-B, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT to amend the general business law and the insurance law, in
        relation to requiring peer-to-peer car sharing programs  provide
        certain insurance coverage"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This  bill  would  reduce  minimum insurance coverage requirements for
cars used by peer-to-peer car sharing services. The bill would also make
other technical changes  to  existing  law,  including  authorizing  the
Department  of  Financial Services to provide a limited license to peer-
to-peer car sharing administrators to offer additional liability, health
and accident, or personal  effects  insurance  coverage  to  shared  car
owners and shared car drivers.

  I  commend  the  Legislature for passing this bill, which, by reducing
the required insurance coverages for peer-to-peer car sharing  vehicles,
will  ultimately make using such vehicles more affordable for consumers.
New York currently has by far the highest minimum insurance requirements
in the country. This bill will bring such requirements more in line with
other states while still providing adequate protections to consumers.
 
  While the bill is intended to authorize the  Department  of  Financial
services  to provide limited licenses to peer-to-peer car sharing admin-
istrators to offer additional insurance to shared car owners and  shared
car drivers, it does not actually include references to peer-to-peer car
sharing  administrators,  the shared vehicle, shared vehicle owners, and
shared vehicle drivers. I have reached an agreement with the Legislature
to include these references so that there  is  no  confusion  about  the
Department's  scope  of  authority. On the basis of this agreement, I am
pleased to sign this bill into law.
 
  This bill is approved.                         (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                                ______

summary: Requires peer-to-peer car sharing programs provide insurance coverage in amounts equal to the financial responsibility requirements set forth in section three hundred eleven of the vehicle and traffic law; removes requirements relating to requiring additional insurance coverage.
